name: AI Now Institute
what: AI Now Institute is an independent research institute producing policy research on AI's social consequences, corporate power, surveillance and public accountability.
tags: AI; research; policy; public interest
source: Homepage and recent update at https://ainowinstitute.org/publications/double-agents; activity also at https://ainowinstitute.org/news/palantir-hires-a-former-democratic-senator-as-it-faces-scrutiny-in-new-congress (verified 2026-11-10).

name: American Foundation for the Blind
what: The American Foundation for the Blind is a US nonprofit expanding opportunities for people who are blind or have low vision through advocacy, research, accessible technology and professional services. It was founded in 1921.
tags: accessibility; blindness; vision loss; nonprofit

name: Ballotpedia
what: Ballotpedia is a non-profit digital encyclopedia of American politics covering elections, candidates, offices and ballot measures. It has 758,643 encyclopedic articles and says it has had more than 1.2 billion page views since 2007.
tags: elections; politics; reference; voting

name: Beeck Center for Social Impact and Innovation
what: Beeck Center for Social Impact and Innovation is the Beeck Center for Social Impact and Innovation at Georgetown University works to build a people-centred, digitally enabled government, connecting government and the civic tech ecosystem through research, networks and practical tools. It was founded in 2014.
tags: govtech; research; public interest technology; university

name: Benetech
what: Benetech is a nonprofit building accessible education technology, including Bookshare and its Global Certified Accessible programme. It campaigns to make accessibility the norm in schools and institutions.
tags: accessibility; education; software for good; nonprofit
source: Homepage and recent update at https://benetech.org/csun-2026-accessibility-ai-title-ii-benetech/; activity also at https://benetech.org/blog/ (verified 2026-11-10).

name: CarbonPlan
what: CarbonPlan is a non-profit that analyses climate solutions, focusing on carbon offsets, carbon removal, and climate risk. It publishes open data and tools including OffsetsDB and Open Climate Risk.
tags: climate; open data; research; tools

name: Center for Civic Design
what: Center for Civic Design is an US non-profit that applies plain language, accessibility, information design and research to election materials and voter journeys. It publishes free tools, field guides and research for election officials.
tags: elections; design; accessibility; research

name: Center for Tech and Civic Life
what: Center for Tech and Civic Life (CTCL) is a nonpartisan nonprofit modernising US election administration through grants, research, training and data tools. Its projects include the Ballot Information Project and Governance Project.
tags: elections; civic tech; grants; research

name: Code for America
what: Code for America is a US civic-tech nonprofit that works with governments to make public benefits and services easier to access, including SNAP, tax credits and criminal record relief.
tags: civic tech; government; digital services; nonprofit

name: CodeAI
what: CodeAI is an education nonprofit, formerly Code.org, working so every K-12 student can learn AI and computer science. It provides free curriculum, teacher training and policy work, and says it has reached 155 million students and 3 million teachers in 190 countries.
tags: computer science; education; K-12; AI

name: Coding it Forward
what: Coding it Forward is a nonprofit that builds civic tech career paths for early-career technologists and places them in government agencies and nonprofits through its Fellowship.
tags: public interest technology; fellowship; students; civic tech
source: Homepage and recent update at https://www.codingitforward.com/s/DC-Department-of-Human-Services-Fellow-Report.pdf; activity also at https://www.codingitforward.com/ (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Community Solutions
what: Community Solutions is a nonprofit working with more than 150 cities and counties through Built for Zero to reduce homelessness using real-time data and coordinated action.
tags: homelessness; housing; data; nonprofit

name: Crisis Text Line
what: Crisis Text Line provides free, 24-hour, confidential text support for people in crisis. It says it has supported over 11 million conversations in the US since 2013.
tags: mental health; crisis support; text messaging; nonprofit

name: Data & Society Research Institute
what: Data & Society is an independent nonprofit research institute studying the social implications of data, automation and AI, producing research to ground public debate and technology policy.
tags: research; technology policy; data; society

name: DataKind
what: DataKind works with social impact organisations to design data science and AI projects, and builds shared products such as its Beacon community data platform. It also runs the Data for Good movement and education initiatives.
tags: data science; nonprofit; volunteers; AI
source: Homepage and recent update at https://www.datakind.org/2026/06/17/introducing-beacon-a-new-platform-for-community-data-coordinated-action/; activity also at https://www.datakind.org/blog/ (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Democracy Works
what: Democracy Works is a non-partisan nonprofit that builds voter engagement and election data tools, including TurboVote, the Elections API, and the Voting Information Project.
tags: voting; elections; civic tech; information

name: Election.org
what: Election.org is a nonpartisan civic reference publishing source-linked records on US elections, candidates, elected officials, campaign finance and local government. It provides charts, downloads and documented data endpoints.
tags: civic tech; elections; public data; civic education
source: Homepage and recent update at https://election.org/data (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Electronic Frontier Foundation
what: Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) is a nonprofit defending civil liberties in the digital world through litigation, policy analysis, grassroots activism and technology development.
tags: digital rights; privacy; free speech; surveillance

name: EveryoneOn
what: EveryoneOn is a US digital inclusion nonprofit connecting under-resourced communities to affordable internet, computers and digital skills training, with place-based work in California and Milwaukee.
tags: digital inclusion; affordable internet; devices; digital skills
source: Homepage and recent update at https://www.everyoneon.org/s/Everyone-On-2025-Impact-Report.pdf; activity also at https://www.everyoneon.org/blog-posts/q3update (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Feeding America
what: Feeding America is the largest hunger-relief organisation in the United States, a national network of 250+ food banks, 20+ state associations and 60,000+ agency partners. It distributes food and advocates on hunger policy.
tags: food security; food banks; hunger; nonprofit

name: Freedom of the Press Foundation
what: Freedom of the Press Foundation is a nonprofit that builds and supports secure journalism tools including SecureDrop and Dangerzone, runs the U.S. Press Freedom Tracker, and campaigns on press freedom.
tags: press freedom; journalism; security tools; encryption

name: GovTrack
what: GovTrack is an independent project tracking US Congress legislation and votes plus White House actions. It publishes bill status, voting records, statistics and analysis.
tags: congress; legislation; transparency; open data

name: ImpactLine
what: ImpactLine is a free public-budget reader that organises government revenue and spending with source links and fiscal periods. Its site covers the federal government, all 50 states and 35,395 local governments.
tags: civic tech; fiscal transparency; public budgets; public records

name: Kapor Center
what: Kapor Center is a family of organisations, including Kapor Foundation, SMASH, Kapor Capital, Kapor Advocacy and the P.R.I.M.E. Alliance, working to remove barriers for people of colour in tech through research, programmes, advocacy and investment.
tags: racial equity; tech sector; research; investment

name: Knowbility
what: Knowbility is an Austin-based nonprofit that runs accessibility training, consulting and usability testing, including the Accessibility Internet Rally and the John Slatin AccessU conference. It was founded in 1999.
tags: accessibility; disability; training; consulting
source: Homepage and recent update at https://knowbility.org/programs/air (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Open States
what: Open States publishes standardised legislative data for all 50 US states, Washington DC, Puerto Rico, and Congress through a website, API, and bulk downloads. It has been run by Plural since 2021.
tags: state legislatures; open data; legislation; api

name: ProPublica
what: ProPublica is an independent, non-profit investigative newsroom producing public-interest journalism. Its investigations are published free online and often include datasets, tools and legal action to obtain records.
tags: investigative journalism; nonprofit news; public interest

name: Public Knowledge
what: Public Knowledge is a policy nonprofit working on freedom of expression, an open internet, affordable communications and creative works. Its current issues include broadband access, copyright reform and trustworthy AI.
tags: internet policy; open internet; free expression; advocacy

name: Rewiring America
what: Rewiring America is a US nonprofit working to electrify households and make clean energy affordable, through policy, data tools and community programmes.
tags: electrification; clean energy; households; climate

name: U.S. Federation of Worker Cooperatives
what: The U.S. Federation of Worker Cooperatives is the national grassroots membership organisation for worker cooperatives and democratic workplaces. It says its members represent an estimated 1,300 US worker co-ops and their 15,000 workers.
tags: worker cooperatives; economic democracy; membership; advocacy

name: USAFacts
what: USAFacts is a nonpartisan civic initiative founded by Steve Ballmer that turns government data into free articles, reports and tools; it is privately funded and takes no advertising or external donations.
tags: open data; government data; statistics; nonpartisan
source: Homepage and recent update at https://usafacts.org/reports/government-10-k/; activity also at https://usafacts.org/ (verified 2026-11-10).

name: Vote.org
what: Vote.org is a nonpartisan nonprofit using technology and outreach to help Americans register, check registration, request mail ballots and find voting information. It says it has helped more than 40 million people get election-ready.
tags: voting; registration; elections; nonpartisan
